sections.heading: 1. Choosing and switching
lines: ① Jog in the shop, pick the comfiest.
② Match it to trails, treadmill or road.
③ Big change? Mix old and new for a few weeks.
④ Log kms in your app, rotate two pairs.

sections.heading: 2. It may not be the shoes if…
lines: Pain keeps coming back or you limp after —
check training load and strength first.

slides.title: When it's not the shoes
slides.bubble:
Causes differ for everyone.
An assessment comes first!
slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Toto spent half an hour staring at the shoe wall. No shoe will make you injury-proof, but the right one can make running feel a lot better 👟

A good starting point is comfort. Research suggests the shoe that feels comfortable from the first few steps is a sensible pick for most runners. Match it to the running you actually do, and if you're switching to something very different, like much lower drop, mix old and new pairs for a few weeks.

If a niggle keeps coming back, it's usually about training load, strength and recovery rather than the shoe itself. Our Chatswood physios look at the whole picture, not just your feet. Book online via the link in bio.

General information only — not a substitute for an individual assessment.
